title: Function to create contigency tables — ContigencyTables
text: Response.data scored item responses matrix form matrix data frame. matrix include variables (group, stratum, cluser, etc.). Response.code numerical vector possible item responses. default, Response.code=c(0,1). Group variable group membership (e.g., gender). length equal sample size item response matrix. group.names Names defined group (e.g., c('Male','Female')). argument optional. default, group.names=NULL. provided, group names "Group.1, Group.2, etc." automatically generated. Stratum matching variable. default, Stratum=NULL. provided, observed total score used. Cluster cluster variable. length equal sample size item response matrix. default, Cluster=NULL. variable used generate contigency tables. included returned data set DIF analysis. missing.code Indication missing values defined data. default, missing.code="NA". missing.impute approach selected handle missing item responses. default, missing.impute="LW", indicating list-wise deletion used. options include: "PM" (person mean row mean imputation),"IM" (item mean column mean imputation), "TW" (two-way imputation), "LR" (logistic regression imputation), EM (EM imputation). Check package "TestDataImputation" (https://cran.r-project.org/package=TestDataImputation) details.  Note. missing data detected group, cluster, stratum variables, listwise deletion used handling missing item responses. print.information Indicator whether function running information printed screen. default, print.information=TRUE.

title: Function to create contigency tables — ContigencyTables
text: list strata statistcs, contigency tables, etc. Strata.stats Summary statistics item: n.valid.strata, n.valid.category, also sample sizes stratum across items. c.table.list.list contains contigency tables across items strata. c.table.list.valid list contains valid contigency tables across items strata. Strata missing item response categories zero marginal means removed. data.cleaned data set variables "Group",  "Group.factor","Cluster", "Stratum", item responses (missing data handled).

text: main function computes unadjusted adjusted MH statistics presence clustered data based Begg (1999) <doi:10.1111/j.0006-341X.1999.00302.x>, Begg & Paykin (2001) <doi:10.1080/00949650108812115>, French & Finch (2013) <doi: 10.1177/0013164412472341>.

title: Main function to compute adjusted Mantel-Haenszel statistics — ML.DIF
code: ML.DIF (Response.data, Response.code=c(0,1),Cluster, Group,         group.names=NULL, Stratum=NULL, correct.factor=0.85,         missing.code="NA", missing.impute="LW",         anchor.items=NULL, purification=FALSE,         max.iter=10, alpha = .05)

title: Main function to compute adjusted Mantel-Haenszel statistics — ML.DIF
text: Response.data scored item responses matrix form matrix data frame. matrix include variables (group, stratum, cluser, etc.). Response.code numerical vector possible item responses. default, Response.code=c(0,1). Cluster cluster variable. length equal sample size item response matrix. Group variable group membership (e.g., gender). length equal sample size item response matrix. group.names Names defined group (e.g., c('Male','Female')). argument optional. default, group.names=NULL. provided, group names "Group.1, Group.2, etc." automatically generated. Stratum matching variable. default, Stratum=NULL. provided, observed total score used. correct.factor value adjustment applied adjusted MH statistic (.e., f). default value used .85. adjusted MH statistic found exhibit low statistical power DIF detection conditions. One solution reduce magnitude f multiplying correct factor (e.g., .85, .90, .95). value .85 suggested French & Finch (2013) <doi: 10.1177/0013164412472341>. missing.code Indication missing values defined data. default, missing.code="NA". missing.impute approach selected handle missing item responses. default, missing.impute="LW", indicating list-wise deletion used. options include: "PM" (person mean row mean imputation),"IM" (item mean column mean imputation), "TW" (two-way imputation), "LR" (logistic regression imputation), EM (EM imputation). Check package "TestDataImputation" (https://cran.r-project.org/package=TestDataImputation) details.  Note: missing data detected group, cluster, stratum variables, listwise deletion used handling missing item responses. anchor.items scored item responses matrix selected anchor items. matrix subset response data matrix specified . default, anchor.items=NULL. purification True false argument, indicating whether purification used. default, purification=FALSE.  Note: Purification applied anchor items specified /matching variable defined. max.iter maximum number iterations purification. default value 10. alpha alpha value used decide DIF items. default value .05.

title: Main function to compute adjusted Mantel-Haenszel statistics — ML.DIF
text: list MH statistcs, contigency tables, etc. MH.values Summary estimated MH statistics corresponding p-values. Specifically,   * MH.unadj unadjusted MH test statistic.  * MH.score MH statistic based working score test (Begg, 1999).  * MH.GMH MH test statistic based Holland & Thayer's (1998) formula.   * MH.Yates MH.GMH statistic Yates' correction.   * MH.adj adjusted MH statistic clustered data;   * f.adj adjustment value based Begg (1999).   * f.adj.correct product f correction factor (.85, etc.).   * DIF.Item (Yes) = 1 indicates item flagged DIF item;  * N.Valid, N.Strata, N.Cluster refer sample size, number valid stata cluster used analysis. Stratum.statistics summary statistics item: n.valid.strata, n.valid.category, also sample sizes stratum across items. c.table.list.list contains contigency tables across items strata. c.table.list.valid list contains valid contigency tables across items strata. Strata missign item response categories zero marginal means removed. data.cleaned data set variables "Group",  "Group.factor","Cluster", "Stratum", item responses (missing data handled).

"Performance software modified mantel-haenszel statistic correlated data."  Journal Statistical Computation Simulation, 70(2), 175-195. doi:10.1080/00949650108812115. French, B. F. & Finch, W. H. (2013). "Extensions Mantel-Haenszel Multilevel DIF Detection."  Educational Psychological Measurement, 73(4), 648-671.  doi:10.1177/0013164412472341. Holland, P. W. & Thayer, D. T. (1988).
